text: Nifty closed green today. But more stocks fell than rose. So who pushed the market up?
Tuesday, November seventeen. Nifty closed at twenty five thousand, three hundred eighty seven, up zero point three eight percent. Sensex added four hundred twenty seven points.
Yet on the BSE, two thousand one hundred forty eight stocks fell, and only two thousand and twelve rose. Smallcaps ended in the red.
And here's the twist. One index closed at a level it has never closed at before.
Bank Nifty. Up one point one three percent, to a record close of sixty two thousand, two hundred seventy three. PSU banks jumped almost two percent. Axis Bank and SBI led the charge.
Why? Crude oil slipped to about ninety one dollars a barrel during the day, easing India's import bill. And foreign investors kept buying India, even after a sharp sell-off on Wall Street.
Not everyone joined the party. IT stocks fell. HCL Tech dropped two percent, and Infosys one point three.
So here's the answer. A few heavyweight banks can lift the whole Nifty, even when most stocks fall. The index alone never tells the full story.
Save this, and follow money in cloud for the market in a minute. Education only, not investment advice. Because a green Nifty doesn't always mean a green market.
